# Policy-KB bijection audit — service_dispatch_desk / task 1

Scope: the published corpus `env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/docs/service/` (65 documents,
sha256 of the file listing `463fc9df9c87fadcbd367f4f09e9d0f0b9698504165d3d861c9b4da20f16d136`)
against `env/env_0002_commercial_hvac_service_contractor/tasks/service_dispatch_desk/service.extended.yaml`
(the base `policies:` section, all six `extended_policies`, every `overwrite`, every `prerequisite`,
every `baseline` and every declared `factor`) and `task_tools.py` as exposed at runtime.
This task is audited on its own; the whole domain of the relevant policy is scanned, not only the
branch this seed hits.

### B. This task's two extended policies — baselines and factor ladders

**`service_ext_credit_ceiling_review`** — baseline in *Working Out the Open Balance Ceiling at
Review* (role baseline). Every element of `baseline.rule` is carried: what the ceiling is worked out
from and that it replaces the ceiling the program carried; "The record is read over the last 12
months" (`standard_review_months` rendered); the starting ceiling at the tier's published credit
limit (named as a published figure); no payment-record step; nothing cut for arrears; no step for
the owner's other accounts; no volume allowance; and the assembly, given twice — once in prose and
once as a numbered "order of the assembly" — with the three steps combined into a single factor and
never applied one after another, the volume allowance added to the product rather than multiplied by
it, and only the total rounded half up. Nothing added.

| Factor | Factor document | Ladder check |
|---|---|---|
| `review_window` (method) | *The Window a Ceiling Review Reads* | All three tiers; both compound conditions (less than a full term, privileges restored or not); both counting rules ("counting each month or part month up to the day of the review"); term length per tier in a full table. |
| `starting_ceiling` (method) | *The Starting Ceiling a Review Works From* | All three tiers; "rounded up to the next whole multiple of 1000 US dollars" (`thousand` rendered); the half-the-limit boundary stated on both sides; published credit limit per tier. |
| `payment_record` (parameter) | *Step for the Account's Payment Record at Review* | All three tiers; counts 8 and 4 and steps 0.15 and 0.08 in figures; both compound conditions; suspension period per tier. |
| `arrears_position` (parameter) | *Cut for Arrears at a Ceiling Review* | All three tiers; cuts 0.25 and 0.10 in figures; tier 2's three-part compound condition intact; suspension period and credit limit per tier. |
| `portfolio_position` (parameter, cross-difficulty) | *Step for the Owner's Maintenance Portfolio at Review* | All three tiers; 20000 threshold and steps 0.12 and 0.05 in figures; the 12-month window named; the Preventive Maintenance Agreements records and the fields read named. |
| `call_volume_allowance` (parameter) | *Allowance for the Account's Call Volume at Review* | All tiers; counts 12, 2 and 6 and allowances 15000 and 7500 in figures; the compound condition of tier 1 and the fall-through to tier 2 expanded correctly in the table. |

**`service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price`** — baseline in *Working Out the Price of a Prepaid
Hour Block*. Carries: what the price is worked out from; "The hours drawn are read over the last 12
months" (`standard_year_months` rendered); the definitions of the prepaid hours standing and the
shortfall, both floored at nil; "sold as a single one of the tier's minimum purchase multiples, that
is 1 multiple" (`one_multiple` rendered); hours sold = multiples × minimum purchase; the whole block
at the tier's block hour rate; no settlement discount; no office release charge; the whole-life open
position "without any window"; the headroom and the excess floored at nil; and the assembly — the
discount worked out on the block price alone and never on the price after the release charge, the
release charge added afterwards, only the total rounded half up. The minimum purchase, expiry period
and block hour rate are named as the figures published for the program, and the credit ceiling as
the one standing on the rate program.

| Factor | Factor document | Ladder check |
|---|---|---|
| `block_size_sold` (method) | *How Large a Prepaid Block the Drawing Record Calls For* | All three tiers; "as many whole multiples as it takes to cover it, rounded up"; the "above one minimum purchase" boundary stated on both sides; minimum purchase per tier. |
| `drawing_record_window` (method) | *The Window a Block Purchase Reads Drawn Hours Over* | All three tiers; both methods with their counting rules; rollover switch, expiry months and term months per tier. |
| `stepped_block_rate` (parameter, cross-difficulty) | *The Rate a Larger Prepaid Block Steps To* | All three tiers; the multiples threshold of 2 and the shares 0.94 and 0.97 in figures; block hour rate per tier; the maintenance records named. |
| `price_basis` (method) | *Pricing a Block Multiple by Multiple* | All three bases; the threshold of 4 and the "unexpired blocks already stand" conjunct; the two-or-three-multiples basis; "Blocks standing unexpired on the program are those bought within the tier's expiry period"; expiry period and minimum purchase per tier. |
| `office_release_rate` (parameter) | *Office Release Charge on a Block Bought Past the Ceiling* | All three tiers; 3.0 and 1.5 percent in figures; the excess defined and floored at nil; where the days past due are counted from. |
| `settlement_record_discount` (parameter) | *Discount a Settlement Record Carries on a Block Purchase* | All three tiers; 2.0 and 1.0 percent in figures; the 12-month ledger window for the charges and payments and the whole-life reading for the open position, stated separately. |

### C. The retired surface

The source declares eight distinct superseded clauses across eleven `overwrite` entries; the two
overwrites that belong to this task's policies are `service_ext_credit_ceiling_review` (none) and
`service_ext_prepaid_block_purchase_price` (the block-drawdown "bought in multiples … oldest block
first" clause). The whole retired surface of the product was checked, since a retirement anywhere
bears on the corpus this task's solver reads:

| Superseded clause | Where it stands retired | Replacement in force |
|---|---|---|
| block drawdown: bought in multiples, drawn oldest block first | *Drawing, Expiry and Refund of Prepaid Hours*, "Terms no longer in force" | *How Large a Prepaid Block the Drawing Record Calls For* (this task) and *Prepaid Hours Standing Against the Hours of a Call* |
| block drawdown: once the block reaches zero, overage rate | same document | the further technicians' element in *Working Out the Labor Line of a Completed Call* |
| labor billing: the multiplier clause | *Pricing a Demand Call on the Ticket* | *Premiums Carried by the Hour Band of a Call* |
| labor billing: the lead/journeyman/apprentice clause | same document | *What a Second Technician on a Call Is Billed At* |
| billing: the invoice falls due the tier's payment term after the invoice date | *Invoicing a Work Order and Applying Payments* | the no-due-day sentences in the labor, late fee and settlement hubs |
| billing: an invoice unpaid past its due day carries the tier's late fee | same document | *Working Out the Month's Arrears Late Fee* |
| guarantee credit: credit rate on the labor charge, capped | *When a Response Guarantee Is Missed* | *Working Out the Credit for a Missed Response* |
| emergency entitlement: surcharge on top beyond the included calls | *The Program Year's Emergency Dispatches* | *What the Program Year's Emergency Dispatches Add to a Settlement* |

Eight declared, eight carried as retired, one-to-one. None is still stated as a rule in force, none
has vanished, and the corpus retires nothing the source did not declare retired. The unnamed clauses
of the same base policies remain carried as clauses in force — for this task most pointedly the
block-drawdown terms that were **not** retired (face value on drawing, expiry, rollover, refund),
all of which stand in *Drawing, Expiry and Refund of Prepaid Hours* under "Terms in force".

One replacement is carried at entailment rather than by a sentence of its own — the source's "The
hours beyond the prepaid balance never carry the further technicians' element, which is billed on
the hours charged for in full …" — and the reasoning is recorded in the task 0 file of this
difficulty, section C. It bears on the labor-line policy, not on either of this task's two.

## kb_to_source

Every normative claim in the 65 documents was traced to a source clause. The classes checked —
eligibility and gates, statuses, time anchors and their counting rules and boundaries, per-tier
figure definitions, the computation baselines, the factor ladders, and the tool hubs' effects,
parameters and receipts — each resolve to a base `policies:` rule and its `eligibility`, to a
`temporal_basis`, to the `parameter_schema`, to a `baseline.rule` sentence, to a `factors[].ladder`
tier, or to a `task_tools.py` contract as printed at unlock. The tool contracts were compared
directly against the two hubs of this task: `set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3` and
`purchase_hour_block_a465dc68` each print parameter descriptions that match the documents' parameter
tables word for word, including the owner statement ("This is the building owner's own act …") and
the receipt.

**Additions found: none.** A sweep for added-policy phrasings ("please confirm", "check with",
"review again", "notify the", "before proceeding", "if it fails, follow", "step 1", "checklist",
"roadmap") returns no match. No document adds a confirmation, a review, a notification, an
exception procedure or an ordering step the source does not have. In particular neither of this
task's hubs asks the desk to confirm the price with the owner, to re-check the ceiling afterwards,
or to verify the purchase order beyond what `block_purchase_order_on_file` requires.

**Omissions found: none.**

**Rewrites found: none.** Two places were examined closely and cleared:

1. *Technician Labor Rate Card* keeps a "Weekend multiplier" column although the clause that billed
   weekend labor that way is retired. Cleared: the card is a facet document defining published
   figures, states no billing procedure, marks its illustration as showing only how the card is
   read, and carries weekend figures identical to the after-hours figures at every tier, so it
   cannot diverge from the in-force *Premiums Carried by the Hour Band of a Call*.
2. The stored program fields `block_hours_remaining: 24.0` and `balance_due: 4750.0` could tempt a
   reader to substitute them for the computed prepaid balance and open position. Cleared: no
   normative sentence names either field as an input. *Working Out the Price of a Prepaid Hour
   Block* defines the prepaid hours standing as "the hours of every block bought within the tier's
   expiry period less the hours drawn over the window read, never below nil" and the open position
   as "everything invoiced on the program over its whole life less every payment received on it over
   its whole life, without any window". The source closes the boundary and the documents close it
   the same way and no further.

**Prerequisite-side specific checks.**

- *Cross-problem operational guidance*: **none**. Six discoverable tool names occur in the corpus,
  each exactly once and each in the hub of the problem that owns it. *Buying a Block of Prepaid
  Technician Hours* names only `purchase_hour_block_a465dc68`; *Writing a Reviewed Open Balance
  Ceiling on a Rate Program* names only `set_program_credit_ceiling_aca954d3`. Neither names the
  other's tool, and no "if unmet, first call …" sentence exists.
- *A task's opening world state written in as a policy fact*: **none**. No document states that a
  ceiling stands unreviewed, that a program's last change was of a particular kind, that a block has
  run dry, or that an account carries a particular open position. Every worked example is marked
  hypothetical and uses invented figures.

## bijection_verdict

**PASS.** No `KB-BIJECTION RED`.

- Every normative atom of the base `policies:` section and of this task's two extended policies —
  including untriggered branches and every tier of every declared factor's ladder — has an
  equivalent prose home.
- Both baselines are carried complete, with their own constants rendered
  (`standard_review_months` as 12 months, `thousand` as "the next whole multiple of 1000 US
  dollars", `standard_year_months` as 12 months, `one_multiple` as "a single one of the tier's
  minimum purchase multiples, that is 1 multiple") and every product figure they read named; the
  ceiling review's assembly order is carried step by step, and the block price's "discount on the
  block price alone, release charge afterwards, only the total rounded" is carried intact.
- All twelve factor ladders of this task are carried in full, tier for tier, with every threshold in
  figures and every compound condition intact; the two cross-difficulty factors name the Preventive
  Maintenance Agreements by their official product name and the kinds of records they read.
- The one prerequisite is carried verbatim, in the declared `state` form, on the blocked side only,
  with connective and strength unchanged, and is resolvable from the sentence, the depended-on
  document and the records.
- The retired surface is one-to-one across the product: eight declared, eight carried as retired.
- Nothing is present in the prose that the source does not require.

Relation to previous revisions: none. This is revision 1 of this file.
